title.zh: 卷二十七 魏書二十七 徐胡二王傳
title.en: Volume 27: Book of Wei 27 - Biographies of Xu, Hu, and the two Wangs
title.raw: 卷二十七 魏書二十七 徐胡二王傳 Volume 27: Book of Wei 27 - Biographies of Xu, Hu, and the two Wangs

sentences.zh: 徐邈 胡質 王昶 王基

translations.literal: Xu Miao; Hu Zhi; Wang Chang; Wang Ji
translations.idiomatic: Xu Miao, Hu Zhi, Wang Chang, and Wang Ji.

sentences.zh: 徐邈字景山，燕國薊人也。

translations.literal: Xu Miao's courtesy name was Jingshan; he was a man of Ji in the Yan princedom.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Miao, courtesy Jingshan, hailed from Ji in the Yan princedom.

sentences.zh: 太祖平河朔，召爲丞相軍謀掾，試守奉高令，入爲東曹議令史。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor pacified the region north of the Yellow River he summoned [Miao] as army strategic adviser to the chancellor, tested him as acting magistrate of Fenggao, then brought him in as deliberation clerk of the eastern bureau.
translations.idiomatic: After Cao Cao subdued Hebei he enlisted Xu Miao as army strategist, tried him as acting magistrate of Fenggao, then appointed eastern bureau clerk.

sentences.zh: 魏國初建，爲尚書郎。

translations.literal: When the Wei state was first founded [Miao] became gentleman of the masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei was founded Xu Miao joined the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 時科禁酒，而邈私飲至於沈醉。

translations.literal: At that time statutes banned alcohol yet Miao drank in secret until stupid drunk.
translations.idiomatic: Though prohibition ruled Luoyang Xu Miao drank himself blind.

sentences.zh: 校事趙達問以曹事，邈曰：「中聖人。

translations.literal: Investigator Zhao Da asked him about bureau business; Miao said 'middle sage.'
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Zhao Da pressed him about office affairs; Xu Miao answered 'the middling sage.'

sentences.zh: 」達白之太祖，太祖甚怒。

translations.literal: Da reported it to the Founding Emperor; the Founding Emperor was very angry.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Da reported to Cao Cao who exploded.

sentences.zh: 度遼將軍鮮于輔進曰：「平日醉客謂酒清者爲聖人，濁者爲賢人，邈性脩慎，偶醉言耳。

translations.literal: general who Estimates the Liao Xianyu Fu advanced saying 'Among habitual drunkards clear liquor is called sage and turbid worthy—Miao's nature is cultivated and cautious—it was but drunken words.'
translations.idiomatic: Xianyu Fu the Estimates-the-Liao general explained tavern slang—clear wine was the sage muddy wine the worthy—and pleaded Xu Miao's sober habits.

sentences.zh: 」竟坐得免刑。

translations.literal: In the end by adjudication he obtained exemption from punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The court let him off.

sentences.zh: 後領隴西太守，轉爲南安。

translations.literal: Later he supervised Longxi grand administrator then shifted to Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Longxi then Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 文帝踐阼，歷譙相，平陽、安平太守，潁川典農中郎將，所在著稱，賜爵關內侯。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen ascended the throne—[Miao] passed through chancellor of Qiao grand administrators of Pingyang and Anping general of the household who directs farming in Yingchuan—wherever he went he gained renown—was gifted secondary marquis within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Under Cao Pi he served Qiao chancellor Pingyang and Anping governors Yingchuan farming general—and earned a secondary marquisate.

sentences.zh: 車駕幸許昌，問邈曰：「頗復中聖人不？

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage visited Xuchang [the emperor] asked Miao 'Have you hit middle sage again?'
translations.idiomatic: Visiting Xuchang Cao Pi asked whether Xu Miao still met the middling sage.

sentences.zh: 」邈對曰：「昔子反斃於穀陽，御叔罰於飲酒，臣嗜同二子，不能自懲，時復中之。

translations.literal: Miao replied 'Formerly Zifan died at Guyang Yushu was punished for drinking—I crave drink like those two and cannot restrain myself—I sometimes hit again.'
translations.idiomatic: Xu Miao cited fatal drunkards Zifan and Yushu admitted his thirst and said he still slipped.

sentences.zh: 然宿瘤以醜見傳，而臣以醉見識。

translations.literal: Yet Suiliu entered tradition through ugliness while your servant is recognized through drunkenness.'
translations.idiomatic: Ugly Suiliu became legend yet Xu Miao claimed fame only as a drunk.

sentences.zh: 」帝大笑，顧左右曰：「名不虛立。

translations.literal: The emperor laughed greatly looked at left and right saying 'The name was not vainly established.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor roared with laughter and told his attendants the reputation was earned.

sentences.zh: 」遷撫軍大將軍軍師。

translations.literal: He was promoted army adviser to the general who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to strategist under the Pacifies-the-Army general.

sentences.zh: 明帝以涼州絕遠，南接蜀寇，以邈爲涼州刺史，使持節領護羌校尉。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming because Liangzhou was utterly distant south bordering Shu bandits appointed Miao inspector of Liang Province bearer of credentials colonel protecting Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cao Rui made Xu Miao Liangzhou inspector—remote frontier facing Shu—with staff and Qiang-colonel rank.

sentences.zh: 至，值諸葛亮出祁山，隴右三郡反，邈輙遣參軍及金城太守等擊南安賊，破之。

translations.literal: When he arrived it happened Zhuge Liang issued from Qishan three commanderies of Longyou rebelled—Miao forthwith dispatched aides-de-camp and grand administrator of Jincheng et al. to strike Nan'an bandits and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He arrived as Zhuge Liang marched from Qishan and Longyou rose; Xu Miao threw aides and the Jincheng governor against Nan'an rebels and broke them.

sentences.zh: 河右少雨，常苦乏糓，邈上脩武威、酒泉鹽池以收虜糓，又廣開水田，募貧民佃之，家家豐足，倉庫盈溢。

translations.literal: West of the river rain was scarce—they constantly suffered lack of grain—Miao memorialized to repair Wuwei and Jiuquan salt ponds to collect barbarian grain moreover broadly opened irrigated fields recruited poor people to tenant them—every household abundant overflowing granaries and treasuries.
translations.idiomatic: Longzhou was dry so Xu Miao rebuilt Wuwei and Jiuquan salt works to trade grain for nomad barley opened paddies for poor tenants until bins overflowed.

sentences.zh: 乃支度州界軍用之餘，以市金帛犬馬，通供中國之費。

translations.literal: Then he assessed what remained beyond military use within the province's borders and with it bought gold silk dogs horses supplying expenses of the central states.
translations.idiomatic: He gauged surplus grain bought silk horses and gold for the capital.

sentences.zh: 以漸收斂民間私杖，藏之府庫。

translations.literal: Gradually collected private clubs from among the people and stored them in the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He slowly confiscated illegal weapons for the armory.

sentences.zh: 然後率以仁義，立學明訓，禁厚葬，斷淫祀，進善黜惡，風化大行，百姓歸心焉。

translations.literal: Then led them with benevolence and righteousness established schools clarified instructions prohibited lavish burial cut excessive sacrifices promoted good dismissed evil—customs transformed on a grand scale—the hundred surnames submitted their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Then he taught ritual ran schools banned wasteful funerals and cults rewarded virtue—the customs turned and the people rallied.

sentences.zh: 西域流通，荒戎入貢，皆邈勳也。

translations.literal: Western regions circulated wild Rong entered tribute—all was Miao's merit.
translations.idiomatic: Trade flowed west tribute arrived—all Xu Miao's doing.

sentences.zh: 討叛羌柯吾有功，封都亭侯，邑三百戶，加建威將車。

translations.literal: Campaigning against rebel Qiang Kewu he had merit was enfeoffed village marquis of the capital precinct three hundred households advanced general who Establishes Might.
translations.idiomatic: He crushed rebel Qiang Kewu earned village marquis of the capital district three hundred households and rank Establishes Might general.

sentences.zh: 邈與羌、胡從事，不問小過；

translations.literal: In conducting affairs with Qiang and Hu Miao did not inquire into petty faults;
translations.idiomatic: With tribes he overlooked petty slips;

sentences.zh: 若犯大罪，先告部帥，使知，應死者乃斬以徇，是以信服畏威。

translations.literal: if they committed great crimes he first informed the tribal chief caused him to know those who should die only then beheaded them to display—therefore they trusted submitted feared awe.
translations.idiomatic: major crimes went first to tribal heads—executions came only after public notice so tribes feared and obeyed.

sentences.zh: 賞賜皆散與將士，無入家者，妻子衣食不充；

translations.literal: Rewards and gifts he distributed all to officers and soldiers—none entered his household—wife and children clothing and food insufficient;
translations.idiomatic: He gave every bonus to the troops—his family went short;

sentences.zh: 天子聞而嘉之，隨時供給其家。

translations.literal: the Son of Heaven hearing approved and supplied his household according to occasion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard and funded his household.

sentences.zh: 彈邪繩枉，州界肅清。

translations.literal: He impeached wickedness and straightened crookedness—the province's borders were cleared.
translations.idiomatic: He purged corruption until Liangzhou ran clean.

sentences.zh: 正始元年，還爲大司農。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengshi he returned as minister of agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengshi 1 brought him back as minister of agriculture.

sentences.zh: 遷爲司隷校尉，百僚敬憚之。

translations.literal: He was promoted metropolitan commander—hosts of officials revered and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: As metropolitan commander he cowed the bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 公事去官。

translations.literal: Public business removed him from office.
translations.idiomatic: Official protocol forced him out.

sentences.zh: 後爲光祿大夫，數歲即拜司空，邈歎曰：「三公論道之官，無其人則缺，豈可以老病忝之哉？

translations.literal: Later he became grand counselor of the palace—within several years then appointment minister of works—Miao sighed 'The three dukes discuss the Way—if there is no fit man the office is left vacant—how can one shame it with old age and illness?'
translations.idiomatic: Made grand counselor then offered minister of works Xu Miao refused: the three excellencies discuss cosmic order—unworthy men leave seats empty—age and illness must not disgrace them.

sentences.zh: 」遂固辭不受。

translations.literal: Thereupon he firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He declined firmly.

sentences.zh: 嘉平元年，年七十八，以大夫薨于家，用公禮葬，謚曰穆侯。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaping age seventy-eight as grand counselor he died at home buried with ducal rites posthumous title marquis Mu.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaping 1 he died at seventy-eight at home as grand counselor with ducal burial and posthumous marquis Mu.

sentences.zh: 子武嗣。

translations.literal: His son Wu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Son Xu Wu inherited.

sentences.zh: 六年，朝廷追思清節之士，詔曰：「夫顯賢表德，聖王所重；

translations.literal: In the sixth year the court recalled gentlemen of pure integrity edict stating 'Displaying the worthy manifesting virtue weighty matters of sage kings;'
translations.idiomatic: Year six honored incorrupt officials: exalting virtue matters to sage kings;

sentences.zh: 舉善而教，仲尼所美。

translations.literal: raising the good and instructing praised by Zhongni.'
translations.idiomatic: lifting good men for instruction Confucius admired.

sentences.zh: 故司空徐邈、征東將軍胡質、衞尉田豫皆服職前朝，歷事四世，出統戎馬，入贊庶政，忠清在公，憂國忘私，不營產業，身沒之後，家無餘財，朕甚嘉之。

translations.literal: Therefore former minister of works Xu Miao east-conquering general Hu Zhi chamberlain Tian Yu all served positions in the former court served through four reigns went out commanding horse entered assisting myriad policies loyal pure at court worrying for the realm forgetting self not managing estates after body perished households had no surplus wealth—we greatly approve.'
translations.idiomatic: The former minister of works Xu Miao, east-conquering general Hu Zhi, and chamberlain Tian Yu all served the prior court through four reigns; whether commanding armies abroad or aiding civil rule at home they were loyal, incorrupt, and selfless, leaving no fortune behind—I deeply commend them.

sentences.zh: 其賜邈等家糓二千斛，錢三十萬，布告天下。」

translations.literal: Gift to Miao and others' households two thousand hu of grain three hundred thousand cash promulgate to all under heaven.'
translations.idiomatic: Grant each family two thousand hu grain thirty thousand cash and publish this empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 邈同郡韓觀曼遊，有鑒識器幹，與邈齊名，而在孫禮、盧毓先，爲豫州刺史，甚有治功，卒官。

translations.literal: Miao's same commandery Han Guan styled Manyou had discernment capacity and repute equal to Miao yet ranked before Sun Li and Lu Yu became inspector of Yu Province had very effective governance died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Fellow townsman Han Guan Manyou matched Xu Miao's reputation preceded Sun Li and Lu Yu governed Yu Province well and died in harness.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏名臣奏》載黃門侍郎杜恕表，稱：「韓觀、王昶，信有兼才，高官重任，不但三州。」〉

translations.literal: 《Memorials of Wei Famous Ministers》 carries attendant at yellow gates Du Shu's memorial stating 'Han Guan Wang Chang truly possess doubled talent high office heavy responsibility not merely three provinces.'
translations.idiomatic: Wei mingchen zou records Du Shu's memorial that Han Guan and Wang Chang deserved higher posts than three provinces.

sentences.zh: 盧欽著書，稱邈曰：「徐公志高行絜，才博氣猛。

translations.literal: Lu Qin authored books praising Miao 'Lord Xu aims high acts pure talent broad spirit fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qin wrote that Xu Miao aimed high lived purely talent wide temper bold.

sentences.zh: 其施之也，高而不狷，絜而不介，博而守約，猛而能寬。

translations.literal: In applying it high yet not narrow pure yet not stiff broad yet keeps restraint fierce yet can be lenient.
translations.idiomatic: In practice lofty but not aloof clean but not stiff learned yet disciplined fierce yet generous.

sentences.zh: 聖人以清爲難，而徐公之所易也。

translations.literal: The sage esteems purity as hard yet what Lord Xu finds easy.
translations.idiomatic: Sages call purity hard Xu Miao wore it lightly.

sentences.zh: 」或問欽：「徐公當武帝之時，人以爲通，自在涼州及還京師，人以爲介，何也？

translations.literal: Someone asked Qin 'When Lord Xu was under Emperor Wu people deemed him accommodating; from Liangzhou and returning to the capital people deemed him rigid—why?'
translations.idiomatic: Why did Xu seem flexible under Emperor Wu yet rigid after Liangzhou

sentences.zh: 」欽荅曰；

translations.literal: Qin replied;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qin answered:

sentences.zh: 「往者毛孝先、崔季珪等用事，貴清素之士，于時皆變易車服以求名高，而徐公不改其常，故人以爲通。

translations.literal: Formerly Mao Xiaoxian Cui Jigui et al. held power esteeming pure plain gentlemen—then all changed carriages and dress seeking lofty reputation yet Lord Xu did not alter his constant—therefore people deemed him accommodating.
translations.idiomatic: Under Mao Jie and Cui Yan pure dress was fashion everyone swapped vehicles for reputation Xu Miao stayed plain so seemed easygoing.

sentences.zh: 比來天下奢靡，轉相倣效，而徐公雅尚自若，不與俗同，故前日之通，乃今日之介也。

translations.literal: Recently all under heaven extravagant turning imitating one another yet Lord Xu elegant conviction as before not same as vulgar—therefore yesterday's accommodation is today's rigidity.
translations.idiomatic: Now fashion runs riot yet Xu Miao stays austere so former flexibility reads as stubborn integrity.

sentences.zh: 是世人之無常，而徐公之有常也。」

translations.literal: This is the world's inconstancy and Lord Xu's constancy.'
translations.idiomatic: The world changed Xu Miao did not.

sentences.zh: 胡質字文德，楚國壽春人也。

translations.literal: Hu Zhi's courtesy name was Wende; he was a man of Shouchun in Chu principality.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zhi courtesy Wende came from Shouchun in Chu.

sentences.zh: 少與蔣濟、朱績俱知名於江、淮間，仕州郡。

translations.literal: In youth together with Jiang Ji and Zhu Ji he was renowned between Yangzi and Huai served province and commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Young he ranked with Jiang Ji and Zhu Ji between Yangzi and Huai and served local office.

sentences.zh: 蔣濟爲別駕，使見太祖。

translations.literal: Jiang Ji was aide-de-camp and caused him to see the Founding Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ji his superior sent him to Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 太祖問曰：「胡通達，長者也，寧有子孫不？

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor asked 'Hu Tongda is a venerable elder—does he have descendants?'
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao asked whether Hu Tongda—Hu Min—had heirs.

sentences.zh: 」濟曰：「有子曰質，規模大略不及於父，至於精良綜事過之。」

translations.literal: Ji said 'There is a son named Zhi—scope and grand strategy does not reach his father—as for refined thorough management of affairs he surpasses him.'
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ji answered Hu Min's son Zhi cannot match his father's vision but handles detail better.

sentences.zh: 〈案

translations.literal: Investigation marker opening annotation.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi opens a note with

sentences.zh: 〈胡氏譜〉

translations.literal: Title Genealogy of the Hu clan.
translations.idiomatic: the heading Genealogy of the Hu lineage.

sentences.zh: ：通達名敏，以方正徵。〉

translations.literal: Colon Tongda's name was Min summoned for rectitude closing citation.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Min style Tongda won recommendation for upright conduct.

sentences.zh: 太祖即召質爲頓丘令。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor thereupon summoned Zhi as magistrate of Dunqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao named Hu Zhi magistrate of Dunqiu.

sentences.zh: 縣民郭政通於從妹，殺其夫程他，郡吏馮諒繫獄爲證。

translations.literal: A county commoner Guo Zheng committed adultery with a cousin-on-mother's-side killed her husband Cheng Ta commandery clerk Feng Liang imprisoned awaiting testimony.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zheng slept with a cousin and murdered her husband Cheng Ta; clerk Feng Liang jailed waited witness.

sentences.zh: 政與妹皆耐掠隱抵，諒不勝痛，自誣，當反其罪。

translations.literal: Zheng and the cousin both endured torture concealing resistance Liang could not bear pain falsely confessed—it should reverse his crime.
translations.idiomatic: Guo and the woman endured the lash in silence until Feng broke and confessed falsely threatening reversal.

sentences.zh: 質至官，察其情色，更詳其事，檢驗具服。

translations.literal: When Zhi reached office he examined their expressions further detailed the affair investigation proved full confession.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zhi read faces reopened the case and extracted true confessions.

sentences.zh: 太祖辟爲丞相屬。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor summoned [Zhi] as aide to the chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao took him as chancellor's aide.

sentences.zh: 黃初中，徙吏部郎，爲常山太守，遷任東莞。

translations.literal: In Huangchu he shifted gentleman of the personnel bureau became grand administrator of Changshan promoted to Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Huangchu brought personnel gentleman Changshan governor then Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 士盧顯爲人所殺，質曰：「此士無讎而有少妻，所以死乎！

translations.literal: Gentleman Lu Xian was killed by someone Zhi said 'This gentleman had no feuds but had a young wife—therefore died!'
translations.idiomatic: When scholar Lu Xian died Hu Zhi reasoned no enemies but a young wife explained the murder.

sentences.zh: 」悉見其比居年少，書吏李若見問而色動，遂窮詰情狀。

translations.literal: He interviewed all neighboring youths young in age clerk Li Ruo when questioned changed color then exhaustively interrogated circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: He questioned young neighbors—clerk Li Ruo flinched under inquiry.

sentences.zh: 若即自首，罪人斯得。

translations.literal: Ruo immediately confessed—the guilty man then obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ruo confessed and the killer was caught.

sentences.zh: 每軍功賞賜，皆散之於衆，無入家者。

translations.literal: Whenever military merit rewards and gifts he distributed all among the multitude none entered household.
translations.idiomatic: Battle bonuses went to the troops never his purse.

sentences.zh: 在郡九年，吏民便安，將士用命。

translations.literal: In the commandery nine years clerks and people convenient and settled officers and soldiers obeyed orders.
translations.idiomatic: Nine years in office brought peace willing clerks and obedient soldiers.

sentences.zh: 遷荊州刺史，加振威將軍，賜爵關內侯。

translations.literal: He was promoted inspector of Jing Province added general who Inspires Might gifted secondary marquis within passes.
translations.idiomatic: He became Jingzhou inspector Inspires Might general secondary marquis.

sentences.zh: 吳大將朱然圍樊城，質輕軍赴之。

translations.literal: Wu great general Zhu Ran besieged Fan city Zhi with light army hurried thither.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ran besieged Fan; Hu Zhi raced there with a light column.

sentences.zh: 議者皆以爲賊盛不可迫，質曰：「樊城卑下，兵少，故當進軍爲之外援；

translations.literal: Debators all thought bandits strong could not be pressed Zhi said 'Fan city is low few troops—therefore ought advance army as outer relief;
translations.idiomatic: Others feared Wu strength Hu Zhi said Fan was low weak needed outside relief;

sentences.zh: 不然，危矣。

translations.literal: if not perilous.'
translations.idiomatic: otherwise it falls.

sentences.zh: 」遂勒兵臨圍，城中乃安。

translations.literal: Thereupon marshaled troops approached the siege within the city then settled.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed the siege lines and steadied the city.

sentences.zh: 遷征東將軍，假節都督青、徐諸軍。

translations.literal: Promoted east-conquering general lent credentials supervised Qing and Xu forces.
translations.idiomatic: He rose east-conquering general with staff over Qing and Xu.

sentences.zh: 廣農積糓，有兼年之儲，置東征臺，且佃且守。

translations.literal: Broadened farming piled grain had stores exceeding one year established east campaign platform both farmed and guarded.
translations.idiomatic: He opened farms stockpiled multiyear grain built the eastern expedition terrace farming while guarding.

sentences.zh: 又通渠諸郡，利舟楫，嚴設備以待敵。

translations.literal: Moreover opened channels in various commanderies benefited boats and oars strictly prepared equipment awaiting enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He dredged harbors for shipping and readied defenses.

sentences.zh: 海邊無事。

translations.literal: Along the sea border nothing happened.
translations.idiomatic: The coast stayed quiet.

sentences.zh: 其爲兄子及子作名字，皆依謙實，以見其意，故兄子默字處靜，沈字處道，其子渾字玄冲，深字道冲。

translations.literal: In making names for elder brother's sons and sons all accorded modest substance to manifest his intent therefore elder brother's son Mo styled Chujing Shen styled Chudao his son Hun styled Xuanchong Shen styled Daochong.
translations.idiomatic: Names for nephews and sons reflected humility Mo Stillness Shen Way sons Hun Dark-Depth Shen Way-Rush.

sentences.zh: 遂書戒之曰：

translations.literal: Thereupon wrote admonishing them saying:
translations.idiomatic: He wrote this warning:

sentences.zh: 夫人爲子之道，莫大於寶身全行，以顯父母。

translations.literal: The way of man being son nothing greater than treasuring body completing conduct to manifest father and mother.
translations.idiomatic: Sons must preserve life and perfect conduct to honor parents.

sentences.zh: 此三者人知其善，而或危身破家，陷於滅亡之禍者，何也？

translations.literal: These three persons know their goodness yet some endanger body destroy household sink into catastrophe of extinction—why?
translations.idiomatic: Everyone praises those aims yet many ruin selves and kin—why

sentences.zh: 由所祖習非其道也。

translations.literal: Because what they model and practice is not the Way.
translations.idiomatic: they imitate the wrong path.

sentences.zh: 夫孝敬仁義，百行之首，行之而立，身之本也。

translations.literal: Filial piety respect benevolence righteousness—first of hundred conducts—practicing them and establishing them root of body.
translations.idiomatic: Filial respect benevolence duty head every virtue foundations of character.

sentences.zh: 孝敬則宗族安之，仁義則鄉黨重之，此行成於內，名著於外者矣。
